Hi Anna — thanks for the packet and timeline. Quick answers and next steps below: 

1) PO routing options for EU customers:
   - Option A (preferred for compliance): Nimbus signs PO to Redwood (Redwood EU Ltd.) and we invoice from our EU entity. This avoids reverse-charge complications and is the fastest path to enable marketplace billing in EU regions.
   - Option B (if you must route to Redwood US): We can accept a US PO but will need VAT reverse-charge paperwork and there may be delays for EU marketplace activation.

2) Required onboarding docs to avoid hold-ups:
   - Legal entity registration (local certificate of incorporation)
   - EU VAT registration certificate (if invoicing EU entity)
   - Bank details and proof of account name (bank statement or bank letter)
   - W-8/W-9 equivalent (tax form) if routing to US entity

I've attached our internal PO routing matrix and a short vendor intake checklist so you can map to the Nimbus packet.

Attachments: redwood_po_routing_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Can you please:
- Confirm which of the two PO routing options Nimbus prefers?
- Upload the entity + VAT docs to the Drive link below so our finance team can pre-validate before the DocuSign step.

Anna/Mina — looping in a couple of operational details from finance: 

- If Nimbus goes with Option A (Redwood EU invoicing), please make sure the VAT certificate explicitly lists the billing entity and VAT number. A pdf of the VAT cert plus a recent bank statement (showing account name and IBAN) will suffice.
- For marketplace listing (AWS/GCP/Azure) we also need the entity name exactly as it should appear in the marketplace profile — mismatch here causes certificate re-submission delays.

I've uploaded the PO routing matrix we use to map marketplace flows across clouds and countries — this will show the delay windows for each option.
